title: GPU sourcing runbook: batch windows and holdback strategy
body:
Purpose:
This sheet is a tactical runbook for staggering GPU orders across regional windows, implementing a 10–25% holdback buffer, and coordinating cross-dock staging to reduce arrival spikes. Intended audience: infra procurement, capacity planning, SRE oncall.

High-level principles:
- Spread large tranches across multiple windows (week buckets) to reduce peak receiving and enable faster validation.
- Maintain a minimum holdback per SKU (10% for standard SKUs, 20–25% for newest H100 runs) until smoke testing completes.
- Route test/validation batches to single staging racks (cross-dock) before distributing to regions.
- Prioritize replacements for high-burn regions (US-WEST, EU-WEST) then backfill lower-burn (APAC).

Quick reference SKUs (internal names):
- A100-80GB (a100-80) — steady-state; alt suppliers available.
- H100-80GB (h100-80) — newest; longer leadtimes, higher failure variance.
- L40-48GB (l40-48) — specialized workloads; moderate leadtime.
- L4-24GB (l4-24) — edge/low-cost; fast delivery windows.

Order cadence matrix (example plan for next 12 weeks):
Week,Region,SKU,Planned order qty,ETA (weeks),Supplier leadtime range,Window type,Holdback%
Wk45,US-WEST,h100-80,160,14-18,14-18,validation-first,25
Wk46,EU-WEST,h100-80,120,14-18,14-18,standard-stagger,20
Wk47,US-EAST,a100-80,300,8-12,8-12,bulk,10
Wk48,APAC,l4-24,200,6-10,6-10,rapid-fill,10
Wk49,US-WEST,a100-80,180,8-12,8-12,replenish,10
Wk50,EU-WEST,l40-48,60,10-14,10-14,validation-first,15

Inventory policy notes:
- Coverage target: maintain 8–12 weeks of burn in each region for core SKUs. For H100 we target 6–8 weeks until vendor stability proven.
- Coverage formula (quick): coverage_weeks = available_units / average_weekly_burn. Update average_weekly_burn from telemetry weekly.
- Safety holdback explained: holdback quantity = ceil(planned_order_qty * holdback%). Holdbacks are quarantined in staging for QA/smoke and only released after acceptance.

Staging / cross-dock flow (operational steps):
1) Shipments arrive to cross-dock staging facility (region-specific where possible).
2) Inventory ops tag shipments with batch-id + supplier lot + expected burn region.
3) Run 48–72h smoke: boot, dmesg check, passthrough stress test (use infra/eval-runner #gpu-smoke).
4) Release policy: pass -> release to regional pool; fail -> quarantine + ticket to supplier RMA channel.
5) Release cadence: nightly releases for bulk orders, same-day for small rapid-fill windows.

Risk matrix and mitigations:
- Supplier leadtime spike: maintain 2-week fallback buffer from secondary supplier for A100 and L4 SKUs.
- Bulk arrival QC failures: cap single-tranche arrivals to 300 units for non-validated suppliers.
- Customs/regulatory hold: add 1–3 weeks contingency for APAC sea shipments (mark in cost-of-arrival).

Operational checklist before placing tranche order:
- Confirm open capacity (SLOs) and burn forecast for target region (ops: capacity-forecast link).
- Ensure staging racks freed to at least X slots (X = planned_order_qty * 0.35).
- Assign oncall + QA owner for batch window.
- Confirm vendor RMA SLA & return slots for that month.

Monitoring and Metrics to update weekly (columns we track in dashboard):
- avg_leadtime_by_supplier (weeks)
- failed_smoke_pct (per supplier lot)
- regional_coverage_weeks (per SKU)
- inbound_packing_eta_variance (days)
- staged_holdback_qty (units)

Open questions / decision points:
- Do we raise holdback for H100 to 30% for first two tranches from new supplier? (recommended: yes if vendor unvetted)
- Should APAC use a single monthly bulk vs two staggered windows to reduce customs friction? (ops preference: staggered)

Action items (owners):
- Avery: finalize supplier SLA table and add to procurement sheet (due: 2024-11-20).
- Devon: validate smoke test automation and add pass/fail hooks to inventory system (due: 2024-11-18).
- Priya: confirm cross-dock staging capacity for Nov–Dec (due: 2024-11-17).

Notes / history:
- Derived from Nov 2023 procurement experiments where single-week arrivals caused 4–6 day distribution delays.
- Lessons: staggered windows reduced ops backlog by ~35% in pilot.

Appendix (quick formulas and commands):
- compute coverage: python -c "print(math.ceil(avail/weekly_burn))" (we store weekly_burn per SKU in infra-metrics).
- smoke test job: infra/eval-runner --job gpu-smoke --batch ${BATCH_ID} --timeout 7200

End of runbook. Keep this doc as a working sheet; update as we gain vendor stability.
